nodes.title: Trust that every result reflects only what was knowable on each date, including companies that were later delisted.
Know the data is correct, through checks and an independent cross-check whose results I can see.
Explore the data myself: any ticker's history, its corporate actions (splits, dividends, delistings), and failed checks.
Build each later research stage on the same trusted data, without redoing data work.

A full download run fetches daily bars, corporate actions and membership history for every company that was an S&P 500 member on any trading day from 2000-01-03 to the most recent completed trading day.

criteria: Given an empty local store, when the user starts a full download run and it completes, then every company with at least one day of membership in the covered period has daily bars, corporate actions and membership intervals stored.
Given the completed run, when the user looks up a company that was removed from the index and later delisted, then its full history up to its last trading day is present.

nodes.title: A refresh run fetches only days and records added or revised since the last completed run.

criteria: Given a completed run as of day D, when the user starts a refresh on day D+5, then the new bars for the days after D are stored and earlier unchanged records are not downloaded again.

Given the primary source revised a past record (for example a late dividend), when a refresh runs, then the revision is stored as a new record with the date it was first seen, and the earlier value is kept.

nodes.title: Each completed download or refresh run produces a new data version with an identifier, a completion time and the date range it covers.

criteria: Given two completed runs, when the user lists data versions, then both appear with identifier, completion time, covered range and record counts.
Given an existing data version, when a later run completes, then reading the earlier version returns exactly the same records as before.

nodes.title: An interrupted or failed run leaves the latest completed data version unchanged.

criteria: Given a run that fails at 60%, when the user reads data, then they see the previous completed version with no partial records.
Given a failed run, when the user starts a new run, then it resumes without downloading records already fetched in the failed run.

nodes.title: The raw response from each source is kept alongside the stored data, so any stored value can be traced to what the source returned.

criteria: Given any stored bar or corporate action, when the user asks for its origin, then the run, the source and the raw values it was derived from are shown.

nodes.title: The members on a trading day are the companies whose membership interval covers that day, by the change's effective date.

criteria: Given 2008-06-30, when the user asks for the members, then Lehman Brothers is among them.
Given a company added effective day D, when the user asks for members on D−1 and on D, then it is absent on D−1 and present on D.

nodes.title: Every company stores all of its membership intervals, so a company that left and rejoined the index has more than one.

criteria: Given a company removed in 2010 and re-added in 2015, when the user views it, then two intervals with their start and end dates are shown.

nodes.title: Every company that stopped trading records its last trading date and its exit type: acquired, bankrupt or liquidated, moved to another exchange, or other.

criteria: Given a company acquired for cash, when the user views it, then its last trading date and the exit type "acquired" are shown.
Given a company still trading, when the user views it, then no exit is shown.

nodes.title: The member count is available for every trading day in the covered period.

criteria: Given any trading day, when the user asks for the member count, then a number is returned, and days outside 498–505 are reported by checks (CHECK-06).

nodes.title: Each company has unadjusted daily open, high, low, close and volume for every trading day it traded in the covered period.

criteria: Given a company and a trading day it traded, when the user asks for its bar, then the five values as traded that day are returned.

nodes.title: Each company has a daily total return, computed from unadjusted closes, splits and cash dividends by their ex-dates.

criteria: Given a 2-for-1 split on day D with no price change, when the return for D is computed, then it is 0% (within 0.01 percentage points), not −50%.
Given a $1 cash dividend with ex-date D on a $100 stock that closes at $99 on D, when the return for D is computed, then it is 0% (within 0.01 percentage points).

nodes.title: Adjusted prices are derived from the daily total returns, anchored to the unadjusted close on a reference date the caller chooses, defaulting to the latest day in the data version.

criteria: Given a split after date T, when adjusted prices are requested anchored at T, then prices up to T equal the unadjusted prices.

nodes.title: The last bar of a company that stopped trading is its last trading date; no prices or returns exist after it.

criteria: Given a company with last trading date L, when bars after L are requested, then none are returned, and the exit type is reported with the response.

nodes.title: A completeness check fails for each trading day in a company's trading life (first bar to last trading date) with no bar.

criteria: Given a company missing its bar on one exchange trading day, when checks run, then exactly one failure names that company and day.

nodes.title: A bar-consistency check fails for each bar where low > min(open, close), high < max(open, close), any price ≤ 0 or volume < 0.

criteria: Given a bar with high below close, when checks run, then a failure shows the bar's five values.

nodes.title: An extreme-move check fails for each daily total return beyond ±50% on a day with no corporate action.

criteria: Given a −60% return on a day without a split or dividend, when checks run, then a failure is recorded; given the same move on a 1-for-2 reverse-split day explained by the split, then none is.

nodes.title: A split-consistency check fails for each split where the ratio of the unadjusted close before and on the ex-date differs from the split ratio by more than 30%.

criteria: Given a 3-for-1 split where the unadjusted price did not change, when checks run, then a failure names the split.

nodes.title: A member-coverage check fails for each trading day on which an index member has no bar.

criteria: Given a member with no bar on a day it was in the index, when checks run, then a failure names the member and day.

nodes.title: A member-count check fails for each trading day with fewer than 498 or more than 505 members.

criteria: Given a day with 490 members, when checks run, then a failure shows the day and the count.

nodes.title: A point-in-time check fails for each record whose first-known date is later than the date it is used for in any as-of read.

criteria: Given a dividend first seen on day K with ex-date before K, when checks run on as-of reads before K, then no read before K returns it; any that does is a failure.

nodes.title: A uniqueness check fails for each company and day with more than one bar, and for each ticker held by two companies on the same day.

criteria: Given a duplicated bar, when checks run, then one failure names the company and day.

nodes.title: A reference-list check compares the user's list of 10 delisted former S&P 500 members against the data, and fails for each field that differs: membership start and end dates, last trading date and exit type.

criteria: Given the user's list with expected values, when checks run, then each of the 10 companies shows pass, or a failure stating the expected and found value.
Given a company on the list that is missing from the data, when checks run, then a failure says it was not found.

nodes.title: The user can mark a failure explained with a note; the explanation stays attached while a later run finds the same failure with the same found values.

criteria: Given an explained failure, when the next check run finds it unchanged, then it shows as explained with the original note.
Given an explained failure whose found values change in a new data version, when checks run, then it shows as failed again, with the old note visible.

nodes.title: Each check run produces a summary per check: failures, explained failures and unexplained failures.

criteria: Given a completed run, when the user opens its summary, then every check is listed with its three counts; the run is "clean" only when unexplained failures are 0.

nodes.title: Before the extreme-move and member-count thresholds (CHECK-03, CHECK-06) are fixed for use, the first full data version is characterised with the data-analysis skill, given: the question "are these thresholds tight enough to catch errors without flooding the list with real events?", all companies' daily total returns and daily member counts over the covered period, split by decade; producing the distribution and tails of daily returns, the count of days beyond each candidate threshold, the member-count series, and missing-bar rates by year. It passes when the thresholds are confirmed or replaced by values the user approves from that analysis.

criteria: Given the analysis output, when the user reviews it, then the thresholds in use are the ones they approved.

nodes.title: For each company the secondary source covers, the cross-check compares daily total returns on every trading day both sources have.

criteria: Given a company covered by both sources from 2005 to today, when the cross-check runs, then the number of compared days equals the number of days both have.

nodes.title: A company passes the cross-check when its daily total returns differ from the secondary source's by ≤ 0.10 percentage points on ≥ 99% of compared days, and its cumulative total return over the compared period differs by ≤ 1% (relative).

criteria: Given a company whose returns differ by 0.5 points on 3% of days, when the cross-check runs, then it fails, with the worst days listed.

nodes.title: Each compared day with a difference > 1 percentage point is listed individually with both sources' values and any corporate action that day.

criteria: Given a dividend recorded on different ex-dates by the two sources, when the cross-check runs, then both days are listed with the dividend shown.

nodes.title: The cross-check reports its coverage: how many current and how many former members were compared, and which were not covered.

criteria: Given a run, when the user opens the cross-check summary, then it shows covered counts for current and former members, and the list of not-covered companies.
Given fewer than 95% of current members are covered, when the cross-check runs, then the summary marks the cross-check as insufficient.

nodes.title: Cross-check failures are failures of the check run, and can be explained like any other (CHECK-10).

criteria: Given a cross-check failure caused by a known source difference, when the user explains it, then it counts as explained in the run summary.

nodes.title: Every read takes an as-of date and returns only records first known on or before it.

criteria: Given a dividend first seen on day K, when data is read as of K−1, then the dividend is absent; read as of K, it is present.
Given an as-of date T, when bars are read, then no bar dated after T is returned.

nodes.title: Every read takes a data version, defaulting to the latest completed one, and names the version it used in its result.

criteria: Given the same as-of date, request and version, when the read is repeated after later refreshes, then the result is identical.

nodes.title: A universe read returns, for a range of days, each day's members with their bars and total returns.

criteria: Given 2008-01-02 to 2008-12-31, when the universe is read, then companies that were members and later delisted (Lehman Brothers among them) appear on their member days.

nodes.title: A read for a company by ticker resolves the ticker to the company that held it on the as-of date.

criteria: Given a reused ticker, when it is read as of a date before the reuse, then the original company's data is returned.

nodes.title: A read for days outside the version's covered range is refused, with the covered range in the error.

criteria: Given a version covering 2000-01-03 to 2026-10-16, when 1999 is requested, then the read is refused naming that range.

nodes.title: The user can start a full download, a refresh or a check run from the app.

criteria: Given no run in progress, when the user starts a refresh, then it begins and appears as running within 2 seconds.

nodes.title: Only one download or refresh run can be in progress at a time.

criteria: Given a refresh running, when the user tries to start another download or refresh, then it is refused with the running run shown.

nodes.title: A running run shows its phase, the companies done out of the total, elapsed time and the errors so far, updated at least every 2 seconds.

criteria: Given a full download in progress, when the user watches the run page, then the done count rises without reloading the page.

nodes.title: The user can cancel a running run; a cancelled run behaves as a failed run (LOAD-04).

criteria: Given a running refresh, when the user cancels it, then it stops within 10 seconds and the latest completed version is unchanged.

nodes.title: Every run is kept in a run history with its type, start and end times, outcome and data version.

criteria: Given three past runs, when the user opens the run history, then all three are listed, newest first, each opening its detail.

nodes.title: Closing or reloading the app does not stop a run; reopening it shows the run's current progress.

criteria: Given a running download, when the user reloads the app, then the run page shows the same run still advancing.

nodes.title: The user can search by current or former ticker or company name, including companies that stopped trading.

criteria: Given a delisted company's former ticker, when the user types it, then the company appears in the results with its exit type.

nodes.title: A company page shows a daily price chart over the company's full history, switchable between unadjusted and adjusted prices.

criteria: Given a company with a 2-for-1 split, when the user switches to unadjusted, then the split shows as a halving of the price; adjusted, it doesn't.

nodes.title: The company page chart marks splits, dividends and the last trading date, and shades membership periods.

criteria: Given a company with two membership intervals and a delisting, when the page opens, then both intervals are shaded and the last trading date is marked.

nodes.title: The company page lists all corporate actions with type, ex-date, value and first-known date.

criteria: Given a company with 40 dividends and one split, when the user opens its actions, then 41 rows are listed in date order.

nodes.title: The company page shows the company's ticker history and its check failures, each linking to the failure detail.

criteria: Given a company with two unexplained failures, when the page opens, then both are listed with their check and day.

nodes.title: The company page shows the cross-check comparison: both sources' cumulative returns over the compared period, and the listed days of disagreement.

criteria: Given a covered company, when the user opens the comparison, then both series and the disagreement days from XCHK-03 are shown; for a not-covered company, the page says "not covered by the cross-check".

nodes.title: A checks page shows the latest run's summary and lets the user filter failures by check, company, status (failed, explained, resolved) and date range.

criteria: Given 120 failures, when the user filters by one check and "failed", then only unexplained failures of that check are shown, with the count.

nodes.title: From a failure, the user can write or edit its explanation note.

criteria: Given an unexplained failure, when the user saves a note, then the failure shows as explained and the summary counts update.

nodes.title: A universe page shows the members on a date the user picks, with the count, and the additions and removals effective that day.

criteria: Given 2008-09-22, when the user picks it, then the members, the count and that day's changes are shown.

nodes.title: Every page states the data version it shows.

criteria: Given two data versions, when the user switches version, then every page shows data from the chosen one and names it.

nodes.title: Rebalance dates are the last trading day of each month, from January 2002 to the last month whose following holding month is complete in the data version, and each date's window is the 504 trading days ending on it.

criteria: Given a data version ending 2026-10-16, when the study runs, then the first rebalance date is the last trading day of January 2002 and the last is the last trading day of August 2026, held through September.
Given rebalance date R, when its window is built, then it holds exactly the 504 trading days ending on R.

nodes.title: A member on the rebalance date is eligible when it has a daily total return on at least 252 of the window's 504 days.

criteria: Given a member that joined trading 300 trading days before R, when eligibility is decided, then it is eligible; given one with 200 days, then it is not.
Given any rebalance date, when the study runs, then the report lists the number of members, the number eligible, and each excluded member with its count of window days.

nodes.title: For each rebalance date, the eigenvalues of the eligible members' correlation matrix over the window are reported, with the share of total variance explained by the largest.

criteria: Given a rebalance date, when its structure is reported, then the eigenvalues sum to the number of eligible members (within 1e-6 relative), and the largest one's share is shown.

nodes.title: For each rebalance date, the noise band is the Marchenko–Pastur range for that window's ratio of eligible names to days; eigenvalues above its upper edge are counted as factors.

criteria: Given 480 eligible names and 504 days, when the band is computed, then its edges are those of the Marchenko–Pastur distribution for ratio 480/504 and unit variance, and every eigenvalue above the upper edge is counted.

nodes.title: For each rebalance date, the market-mode removal diagnostic removes the top k principal components, fitted on that window only, and reports the mean absolute off-diagonal correlation of what is left, for k = 1 and k = the factor count from STRUCT-04.

criteria: Given a window, when the diagnostic runs, then the components, scaling and loadings are fitted only on that window's returns; changing any return outside the window leaves the result unchanged.
Given any portfolio in PORT, when it is built, then it uses the window's total returns, never market-removed residuals.

nodes.title: The sample estimate is the sample covariance of the window's daily total returns.

criteria: Given a window, when the sample estimate is built, then it matches the covariance computed directly from the returns within 1e-10 relative.

nodes.title: The shrinkage estimate blends the sample covariance with a constant-correlation target (each name's own variance, every pair at the window's average correlation), with the blend weight estimated from the window's returns.

criteria: Given a window, when the shrinkage estimate is built, then its blend weight lies in [0, 1] and is reported for that date.
Given a window where the sample correlations are all equal, when the shrinkage estimate is built, then it equals the sample covariance within 1e-8 relative.

nodes.title: The denoised estimate replaces the correlation eigenvalues inside the noise band (STRUCT-04) by their average, keeps those above it, restores the diagonal to 1, and scales back to a covariance with each name's sample volatility.

criteria: Given a window, when the denoised estimate is built, then its diagonal equals the sample variances within 1e-10 relative.

Given a window, when the eigenvalues are replaced and before the diagonal is restored, then those above the band edge equal the sample correlation's, the rest are all equal, and their sum is unchanged within 1e-10 relative.

nodes.title: The factor-model estimate uses k principal-component factors plus each name's residual variance, where k is the factor count from STRUCT-04, and at least 1.

criteria: Given a date with 4 eigenvalues above the band edge, when the factor estimate is built, then it uses 4 factors; given a date with none, then it uses 1.

nodes.title: The shrinkage, denoised and factor estimates are positive definite on the full eligible set of every rebalance date.

criteria: Given any rebalance date, when the three estimates are built, then each one's smallest eigenvalue is > 0.

nodes.title: For each of the shrinkage, denoised and factor estimates, a minimum-variance portfolio is the long-only, fully invested weights over the eligible set with the lowest variance under that estimate.

criteria: Given any rebalance date and estimate, when the portfolio is built, then every weight is ≥ 0, the weights sum to 1 within 1e-8, and no feasible long-only portfolio has a lower variance under that estimate by more than 1e-6 relative.

nodes.title: For each of the shrinkage, denoised and factor estimates, an equal-risk-contribution portfolio gives every eligible member the same share of portfolio variance under that estimate.

criteria: Given any rebalance date and estimate, when the portfolio is built, then every weight is > 0, the weights sum to 1, and every member's risk contribution is within 1% (relative) of the average contribution.

nodes.title: For each of the shrinkage, denoised and factor estimates, a hierarchical-risk-parity portfolio allocates by clustering the members on that estimate's correlations and splitting weight between clusters by inverse cluster variance.

criteria: Given any rebalance date and estimate, when the portfolio is built, then every weight is > 0 and the weights sum to 1.

nodes.title: On a subset of the 100 eligible members with the highest average daily dollar volume over the window, minimum-variance portfolios are built for all four estimates, including the sample estimate, with an equal-weight portfolio over the same 100 as their baseline.

criteria: Given a rebalance date, when the subset is chosen, then it uses only closes and volumes within the window, and the 100 names are listed in the report.
Given a date with fewer than 100 eligible members, when the subset is chosen, then it is all eligible members and the report says so.

nodes.title: The baseline is an equal-weight portfolio over the eligible set on each rebalance date.

criteria: Given 490 eligible members, when the baseline is built, then each holds 1/490 at the rebalance close.

nodes.title: Two reference portfolios are reported but are not baselines: equal weight over all members on the rebalance date, and inverse volatility over the eligible set, using each member's sample volatility in the window.

criteria: Given a rebalance date, when the references are built, then both appear in the scorecard marked "reference".

nodes.title: Each portfolio is formed at the close of its rebalance date and held to the close of the next one, with weights drifting with each holding's daily total return; there is no rebalancing within the month.

criteria: Given a holding that rises 10% while the rest are flat, when the next day's weights are computed, then its weight has grown in proportion and the weights still sum to 1.

nodes.title: A holding that stops trading during a holding month counts its returns up to its last trading day; from the next day, its value is spread across the remaining holdings in proportion to their weights.

criteria: Given a holding with last trading date L in mid-month, when the month's returns are computed, then its return on L is included, and from L+1 the portfolio holds only the other names, still fully invested.

nodes.title: Each portfolio's turnover at each rebalance date is half the sum of absolute differences between its new weights and its drifted weights at that close, with names entering or leaving counted in full.

criteria: Given a portfolio whose new weights equal its drifted weights, when turnover is computed, then it is 0; given a complete change of names, then it is 1.

nodes.title: The synthetic panel has 500 names and 504 days of returns generated from 3 planted factors plus independent name-level noise, with the true covariance known, and the same panel is produced on every run.

criteria: Given two runs, when the panel is generated, then the returns are identical.

nodes.title: On the synthetic panel, the noise band counts exactly 3 factors, and the factor-model estimate uses 3 factors.

criteria: Given the panel, when STRUCT-04 and COV-04 run, then both report 3.

nodes.title: On the synthetic panel, the denoised and factor-model estimates are closer to the true covariance than the sample estimate is, measured by the relative Frobenius-norm error.

criteria: Given the panel, when the three errors are computed, then the denoised and factor errors are each below the sample error.

nodes.title: On the synthetic panel, the minimum-variance portfolios built on the denoised and factor-model estimates have a true variance (under the true covariance) within 10% of the true long-only minimum variance.

criteria: Given the panel, when each portfolio's true variance is computed, then it is ≤ 1.10 × the true long-only minimum.

nodes.title: On a synthetic panel with a diagonal true covariance, the equal-risk-contribution portfolio built on that covariance equals inverse-volatility weights, and the hierarchical-risk-parity portfolio equals inverse-variance weights, each within 1e-6 per weight.

criteria: Given the diagonal panel, when both portfolios are built on the true covariance, then each weight matches its known answer within 1e-6.

nodes.title: A study run on real data refuses to report results unless every check in SYNTH-02–SYNTH-05 passes in the same run.

criteria: Given a failing known-answer check, when the study runs, then it stops before the real-data comparison, naming the failed check.

nodes.title: Every structure result, estimate and portfolio weight for rebalance date R uses only data known on R, read as of R.

criteria: Given a rebalance date R, when any return dated after R or any record first known after R is changed, then the weights formed at R are unchanged.

nodes.title: The scorecard ranks every portfolio by the annualized variance of its daily out-of-sample returns over all its holding months, with its difference from its baseline (PORT-05, or the subset baseline for PORT-04) and its average turnover.

criteria: Given a completed study run, when the scorecard is opened, then every portfolio from PORT-01–PORT-06 appears once, ranked from lowest realized variance, with its baseline difference and turnover.

nodes.title: Every difference in realized variance is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, given: the monthly realized-variance series of each compared pair over the same holding months; the comparisons of every portfolio with its baseline, and of the estimators with each other within each portfolio type and within the subset, as one family. A difference passes as more than chance only if it is significant at 5% after correction for the number of comparisons in the family.

criteria: Given a completed study run, when the scorecard is opened, then each difference is marked "significant" or "not significant", with the corrected p-value and the number of comparisons corrected for.

nodes.title: The stability of the results over time is analysed with the data-analysis skill, given: the question "do the estimator and portfolio rankings hold across market regimes?", the per-date spectra, factor counts, shrinkage weights and monthly realized variances; split into 5-year blocks from 2002 and the crisis windows 2007-10 to 2009-03 and 2020-02 to 2020-04. It produces the ranking in each block and window, the factor count and largest-eigenvalue share over time, and how much each portfolio's turnover varies. It passes when the user has reviewed the analysis.

criteria: Given a completed study run, when the analysis is done, then each block and crisis window shows its ranking, and the user's review is recorded.

nodes.title: Each study run writes a report naming its data version and parameters, with the scorecard, the test results, the exclusions and failures, and the spectrum and realized-variance plots; repeating the run with the same data version and parameters gives identical numbers.

criteria: Given two runs with the same data version and parameters, when their reports are compared, then every number is identical.

nodes.title: A spectrum page shows, for a rebalance date the user picks, the eigenvalue spectrum with the noise band, the eigenvalues above it marked as factors, the largest eigenvalue's share, and the eligible and excluded counts.

criteria: Given 2008-09-30, when the user picks it, then the spectrum, the band edges, the factor count and the counts for that date are shown.

nodes.title: A comparison page shows every portfolio's realized variance, its difference from its baseline with the significance mark from EVAL-03, and its turnover.

criteria: Given a completed study run, when the user opens the comparison page, then every scorecard row from EVAL-02 is shown, and the significant differences are visibly distinguished.

nodes.title: Both pages name the study run they show, with its data version and parameters.

criteria: Given two study runs, when the user switches between them, then both pages show the chosen run and name it.

nodes.title: The data covers every company that was an S&P 500 member on any trading day from 2000-01-03 to the latest completed trading day, including those later removed, acquired, bankrupt or otherwise delisted.

criteria: Given the user's 10 delisted former members, when the data is loaded, then all 10 are present (CHECK-09).

nodes.title: Each company has unadjusted daily open, high, low, close and volume over its full trading life within the covered period, not only its membership periods.

criteria: Given a company that left the index in 2012 and traded until 2015, when its bars are read, then bars through 2015 are present.

nodes.title: Corporate actions cover splits (with ratio), cash dividends (with amount and ex-date), ticker changes and delistings (with last trading date and exit type).

criteria: Given a company's history, when its corporate actions are read, then each action has its type, date and value.

nodes.title: Membership history gives, for each company, every interval it was in the S&P 500, by effective date.

criteria: Given any trading day, when membership is read, then exactly the companies whose intervals cover it are returned.

nodes.title: Every stored record carries the date it first became known to the system or the source, whichever is earlier and evidenced; records without an evidenced earlier date use the date first downloaded.

criteria: Given a record first downloaded on day K with no source-provided known date, when its first-known date is read, then it is K.

nodes.title: A company is identified by a permanent identifier independent of ticker, stable across ticker changes and across data versions.

criteria: Given a company that changed ticker twice, when it is read under any of its tickers, then the same identifier is returned.

nodes.title: The independent cross-check source provides daily split- and dividend-adjusted closes for the companies it covers, fetched independently of the primary source.

criteria: Given a cross-check run, when a company is compared, then its secondary values come only from the secondary source.

nodes.title: Data costs stay under $50 a month in total, using the already-paid primary subscription and a free secondary source.

criteria: Checked at architecture: every source and plan used is listed with its monthly cost, summing to < $50.

nodes.title: In the app, a company page with up to 26 years of daily history and the portfolio comparison page each become interactive within 2 seconds, and the universe page and the spectrum page for any date within 1 second.

criteria: Measured on the user's machine against the full data version.

nodes.title: A refresh run covering up to 5 new trading days completes within 10 minutes; a full check run, excluding the cross-check fetch, within 10 minutes.

criteria: Timed on the user's machine with the full data version.

nodes.title: Data and app stay on the user's machine: the app is reachable only from that machine, and nothing is sent anywhere except requests to the two data sources.

criteria: Checked by reviewing every outgoing connection the system makes, and by confirming the app refuses connections from another device on the network.

nodes.title: Requests to the secondary source are rate-limited to at most 1 request per second, and a cross-check fetch never re-requests a company already fetched that day.

criteria: Checked from the run log of a cross-check run.

nodes.title: The primary source's data is never redistributed: it is stored only locally and the app has no export beyond the user's own research code.

criteria: Checked by reviewing that no feature publishes or uploads stored data.

nodes.title: The app's visual direction is set with the frontend-design skill, given: the single researcher exploring trusted market data and research results, the views in EXPL, RUN and RVIEW with the data each shows, and the brief's ask for a distinctive look, local-only. It passes when the user approves the direction before the views are built.

criteria: Checked by the user's sign-off on the design direction.

nodes.title: The app and its backend agree on the shape of every message between them, so a mismatch is caught before the app runs, not at runtime.

criteria: Checked by a change to a message shape on one side failing the build of the other.

nodes.title: A full study run (known-answer checks, every rebalance date, every estimate and portfolio, the scorecard and the report) completes within 60 minutes.

criteria: Timed on the user's machine with the full data version.
